title: Fieldwork data table and class example data sheet
subject: Geography
unit: Summer 1: Physical fieldwork enquiry (Paper 1 Section B)
source: Written for geography/y10 lesson 64 (Fieldwork data table and class example data sheet (portal printable; example data labelled))
intro: Lesson 64: Collecting primary data: quantitative and qualitative. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Run-off on paving: 500 ml poured; about 450 ml ran into the drain within 1 minute (example).

parts.text: Push the tin in evenly to the 3 cm mark
Start the timer as you finish pouring
Stop when no water remains on the surface; record the time

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A time in seconds for one trial

panels.title: Run-off observation
points: Pour 500 ml on a hard surface
Note the direction and any drain

panels.title: Accuracy
points: Start and stop timer the same way

keywords.def: data as numbers, such as times and volumes
a labelled drawing made at the site
how fast water soaks into the ground
how close a measurement is to the true value

questions.q: Why do we repeat each test three times?
questions.a: To spot anomalies and calculate a reliable mean

questions.q: Give one qualitative method for our enquiry.
What do you record on a surface that does not absorb water?
questions.a: No infiltration; observe and measure run-off

questions.q: Core: Complete your fieldwork (or use the class example data sheet if you cannot): three infiltration trials on four surfaces, one run-off observation, two photos and a field sketch. Record in the data table.
questions.a: A complete data table with 12 timings, a run-off measurement, photos and a labelled field sketch

questions.q: Extend: (3 marks, own exam-style) Explain why you used qualitative data as well as quantitative data.
questions.a: Qualitative explains the numbers, e.g. compaction or plant roots; gives context; supports conclusions

questions.q: Stretch: Suggest one improvement to the accuracy of the infiltration test.
questions.a: Mark the 3 cm depth on the tin; use a measuring jug with ml marks; start timing exactly as pouring ends
B) Qualitative. A labelled drawing describes the site: qualitative primary data.
Both: the stopwatch measures how fast; the photo shows why
